summary: Water Stage-2 beatdown. Regular Feraligatr (Giant Wave 160, or 280 with Torrential Heart) is the every-other-turn workhorse; Mega Feraligatr ex (Mortal Crunch 200, 400 vs a pre-damaged target) is the 370-HP finisher. Munkidori is an ability-only engine (cannot attack: Mind Bend needs Psychic, deck has none) that both heals self-damage off Feraligatr AND places it on the opponent's Active to arm Mortal Crunch's +200. Win engine doubles as loss engine: heavy draw + slow clock => deckout is the primary failure mode.

expected_dmg.formula: 200 + (200 if opponent_active.damage_counters >= 1 else 0)  => 400 when opponent Active is pre-damaged
160 + (120 if Torrential_Heart_used_this_turn else 0) => 280 with skill; self-locks: 'can't use Giant Wave next turn'
places 5 damage counters (50) on SELF (putDamageCounter=true); grants +120 to this Pokemon's attacks vs opp Active this turn
moves up to 3 damage counters (30) from 1 of your Pokemon (heal) to 1 opp Pokemon (place). Arms Mortal Crunch and clears Feraligatr self-damage.
UNPAYABLE in this deck (no Psychic energy). 0 attack-options offered across 120 probe games. Munkidori never attacks.

mechanics_verified.note: Rare Candy evolves Totodile DIRECTLY to Feraligatr AND to Mega Feraligatr ex (skips Croconaw). Both Stage2 evolve from Croconaw but Rare Candy accepts them on a Totodile.
Neo Upper Energy (ACE SPEC): on a Basic provides 1 Colorless; on a Stage2 provides 2 Rainbow (every type, 2 units). Lets Mega attack with Neo+1 energy.
Mega Feraligatr ex is megaEx => 3 prizes when KO'd. Meowth ex => 2 prizes. Regular Feraligatr => 1 prize.

early.until: own Stage2 (49 or 939) in play with >=1 {W} attached, OR turn>=4
early.on_plan: by ~T3-4: a Totodile/Croconaw down + (Rare Candy AND a Stage2) or a natural Croconaw in hand; Munkidori benched holding exactly 1 {D}; ideally Budew active T1 vs item decks for item-lock

mid.until: a Feraligatr with 2 {W} (Giant Wave online) OR Mega with W,W,C/Neo
mid.on_plan: Giant Wave (160/280) landed on >=every-other-turn; a 2nd Feraligatr charging so Surfing Beach can rotate a fresh Giant Wave in on the lock turn; Munkidori Adrena-Brain moving Torrential-Heart self-damage onto opp Active

late.until: opponent prizes <= 2 OR Mega online with a pre-damaged target
late.on_plan: Mortal Crunch 400 or Giant Wave 280 every attackable turn; deckCount kept > ~6 via Dudunsparce Run Away Draw and Sacred Ash; do NOT dig further once combo assembled

doctrines.name: A: Regular-Feraligatr engine (workhorse)
doctrines.plan: Run 3x Feraligatr as the primary body: Giant Wave every-other-turn on each, rotate via Surfing Beach so one Giant Wave fires each turn; Torrential Heart +120 for 280 breakpoints; Munkidori shuttles the self-damage. Cheap ([W,W]), 3 copies, 1-prize bodies.
doctrines.discriminating_metric: play_rate[49] high & first_attack_turn early vs play_rate[939]; A wins if energy_attach_share favors 49-line and post_ko_attack_rate stays high without exposing 3-prize Mega

doctrines.name: B: Mega-tank finisher (pre-damage lock)
doctrines.plan: Race Rare Candy Totodile->Mega; keep opp Active pre-damaged (Munkidori Adrena-Brain / prior Giant Wave / Torrential-Heart-then-move) so Mortal Crunch = 400 every turn; 370 HP tanks while Adrena-Brain heals 30/turn. Only 1 copy => fall back to A if prized/KO'd.
doctrines.discriminating_metric: share of Mortal Crunch resolving at 400 (pre-damaged) vs 200; loss_share[prize] from Mega KO (3 prizes). B wins if predamaged_rate high and Mega-KO rate low

doctrines.name: C: Neo-Upper fast-track
doctrines.plan: Attach Neo Upper Energy to the Stage2 (=2 Rainbow) so Mega attacks with Neo + 1 energy, or Feraligatr with Neo alone. Discriminates whether the single ACE SPEC should be saved for Mega (WWC) vs used to speed a Feraligatr.
doctrines.discriminating_metric: energy_attach_share[10] target = 939 vs 49; first_attack_turn delta when Neo lands on Stage2

tensions.balance: search+draw (Poffin/Ultra/PokePad/PokeGear/Lillie's/Lucian) fire freely while deckCount>~12 AND combo not yet assembled; once Stage2+energy assembled OR deckCount<=~8, STOP digging and start recycling (Dudunsparce Run Away Draw, Sacred Ash). The engine's consistency tool is its own deckout clock.

Torrential Heart adds 50 self-damage per use; Adrena-Brain removes only 30/turn => net +20/turn if both fire every turn. Fire Torrential Heart ONLY on a turn Feraligatr actually attacks AND (Feraligatr.hp_remaining after +50 > incoming, OR Munkidori/Surfing-Beach rotation will preserve it). Never on a Giant-Wave-locked / non-attacking turn.

Commit Mega only when a pre-damaged target is guaranteed (Munkidori online with {D}, or opp Active already damaged); a bare Mega attacking for 200 while a Lightning-weak 370-HP 3-prize body sits exposed is a losing trade.

hypotheses.claim: L0 uses abilities unconditionally, so Feraligatr's Torrential Heart self-fires every turn (incl. Giant-Wave-locked / non-attacking turns), stacking 50 self-damage/turn faster than Adrena-Brain clears (30) -> Feraligatr self-KOs (180 HP dies at 4 uses) and, as last Pokemon, loses on the spot.
hypotheses.direction: torrential_heart fires ONLY on turns this Feraligatr uses Giant Wave; self-inflicted-KO count ~ 0
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Gating too hard removes the +120 that turns Giant Wave 160->280 (needed to OHKO 200-HP bodies and to self-generate pre-damage for Mortal Crunch).
hypotheses.scenario: T5: single Feraligatr Active, already 50 self-damage, used Giant Wave last turn (locked this turn), no benched Munkidori with {D}. Engine sees Torrential Heart ability option -> activates -> +50 (now 100) for no attack. Repeat T7, T9 -> Feraligatr dies to its own skill; if it was the last body, immediate loss.
hypotheses.pattern: board-state gate on self-harm ability (implement Sec2b fire-condition)

hypotheses.claim: Self-removal effects (Dudunsparce Run Away Draw shuffles itself into deck; Meowth ex Tuck Tail bounces itself to hand; Torrential Heart) fired as the LAST Pokemon in play = instant loss (no Pokemon in play).
hypotheses.direction: Run Away Draw / Tuck Tail never fire when they are the only Pokemon in play
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Blocking Run Away Draw generally kills a cheap draw+recycle engine that fights deckout; only the last-Pokemon case is catastrophic.
hypotheses.scenario: Board wiped to a lone benched Dudunsparce (Active just KO'd, nothing to promote but Dudunsparce). Engine uses Run Away Draw -> Dudunsparce shuffled away -> no Pokemon in play -> loss. Same with a lone Meowth using Tuck Tail.
hypotheses.pattern: board-state gate (require >=1 other Pokemon in play)

hypotheses.claim: Manual energy attachment is mis-routed to Munkidori (which can never attack) and to other non-payable bodies, starving the Feraligatr line and delaying the first Giant Wave/Mortal Crunch.
hypotheses.direction: energy_attach_share to 47/48/49/939 (Water) >> to 112; Munkidori receives at most 1 {D} and 0 {W}
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Cutting all energy to Munkidori blocks the single {D} it needs for Adrena-Brain (the pre-damage + Feraligatr-heal engine that arms Mortal Crunch's +200).
hypotheses.pattern: deck-specific fueling plan: cap Munkidori at 1 {D}, route {W} to Feraligatr line by type

hypotheses.claim: Giant Wave shows 160 and Mortal Crunch shows 200, but real damage is 280 and 400. L0 (gust/promotion/lethal/energy split) reads DISPLAY damage and so under-values the attackers, mis-targets gust, and mis-orders evolution.
hypotheses.direction: gust/lethal decisions use real formula (Giant Wave 280, Mortal Crunch 400 when pre-damaged); Mortal-Crunch-at-400 rate high
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Insisting on 400 every time (waiting for pre-damage) can pass turns; a 200 Mortal Crunch that KOs is still fine.
hypotheses.pattern: promote real-damage formula to shared perception (_expected_dmg)

hypotheses.claim: Deckout: unconditional search (Poke Pad/Buddy Poffin/Ultra Ball/Pokegear) + draw supporters (Lillie's, Lucian) every turn empties a 60-card deck before the slow (every-other-turn) clock wins.
hypotheses.direction: loss_share[deckout] below L0 baseline; search fires ~0 when deckCount <= ~8 or combo already in hand
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Stopping digging too early strands the Stage2/energy assembly and creates non-attacking turns.
hypotheses.pattern: dig-stop when deck thin + activate recycle (Sacred Ash / Run Away Draw)

hypotheses.claim: Lillie's Determination / Lucian shuffle the hand away; fired while holding an assembled combo (Rare Candy + Stage2 + {W}) they destroy the win the turn before it lands.
hypotheses.direction: Lillie's/Lucian do NOT fire when hand contains {Rare Candy AND a Stage2} or 2+ combo pieces
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Never refreshing bricks a dead hand; gate must still allow firing on genuinely low-value hands.
hypotheses.pattern: possession-based firing (skip draw-supporter when combo held)

hypotheses.claim: A non-attacking body (Munkidori, or a Giant-Wave-locked Feraligatr) is left/promoted into the Active spot, producing non-attacking turns; L0 treats a {D}-loaded Munkidori as 'charged' and won't retreat it.
hypotheses.direction: Active = Feraligatr/Mega on attackable turns; Munkidori stays benched (Adrena-Brain works from bench)
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Forcing switches every turn burns Surfing Beach / retreat energy and can expose a fresh Pokemon to gust.
hypotheses.pattern: type-aware charged/wall distinction + post-KO promotion of a payable attacker

hypotheses.claim: Adrena-Brain's counter-move is mis-used: not fired to arm Mortal Crunch (must land on opp ACTIVE), or fired to move counters to a benched opp Pokemon, or not used to clear Feraligatr self-damage.
hypotheses.direction: Adrena-Brain fires when Munkidori has {D} and (Feraligatr carries self-damage OR opp Active needs pre-damage), targeting opp ACTIVE
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Rigidly always dumping onto Active wastes it when Feraligatr has no self-damage to move (nothing to shuttle).

hypotheses.claim: Post-KO promotion picks the highest DISPLAY-damage Pokemon and can promote an un-charged Mega/Feraligatr or a type-dead Munkidori, exposing the 3-prize Mega or wasting a turn.
hypotheses.direction: promote a Water body that can pay an attack next turn; never auto-promote Munkidori; avoid exposing a bare Mega
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Over-constraining promotion can leave no legal high-value promote and default to a worse body.

hypotheses.claim: Ultra Ball (discard 2) and Lillie's discard-equivalents throw away combo pieces (Rare Candy / Stage2 / the scarce 6 {W} / 3 {D}).
hypotheses.direction: Ultra Ball never discards Rare Candy / a needed Stage2 / last energy of a needed type when alternatives exist
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Over-protecting leaves nothing legal to discard, blocking Ultra Ball entirely.
hypotheses.pattern: possession-aware discard; recover via Sacred Ash if lost

hypotheses.claim: Surfing Beach is under-used: the free {W}<->{W} switch should rotate a fresh (non-locked) Feraligatr into Active on Giant-Wave-lock turns instead of passing or paying 3 retreat.
hypotheses.direction: on a Giant-Wave-locked turn with a charged benched Feraligatr, Surfing Beach rotates it in

threshold.value: giant_wave_uptime >= 0.7 when a 2nd charged Feraligatr exists

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Rotating away a healthy Active into a fragile one can invite gust.

hypotheses.claim: Budew (Itchy Pollen, free, item-lock) and Shaymin (Flower Curtain bench protection) are situational techs the engine may mis-deploy (e.g., leaving Budew 30-HP active late as a free KO, or not opening Budew vs item-reliant decks).
hypotheses.direction: Budew active only early/vs item decks then retreated/sacrificed cheaply; Shaymin benched for Flower Curtain
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: Over-restricting Budew loses the T1 item-lock tempo tool.

axes_notes.speed: Slow: needs Stage2 + 2-3 energy; Giant Wave locks every other turn. first_attack_turn late.
axes_notes.power_curve: High ceiling: 280 Giant Wave, 400 Mortal Crunch, 370-HP tank.
axes_notes.consistency: Deep tutor/draw suite (Poffin/Pad/Ultra/Pokegear/Hilda/Petrel/Rare Candy) but must find Stage2+energy+pre-damage.
axes_notes.recovery: Strong: Sacred Ash, Dudunsparce recycle, Meowth Tuck Tail, 3x Feraligatr redundancy.
axes_notes.resource_economy: Weak: only 6 {W} for a Water deck; heavy draw = deckout floor (probe: near-universal deck-empty in long games).
axes_notes.disruption_resistance: Fragile to Lightning weakness (x2 on all Feraligatr incl. 370 Mega), gust onto un-charged bodies, and hand disruption of the combo.
axes_notes.self_harm_management: Torrential Heart self-damage (50/turn) exceeds Adrena-Brain clear (30/turn); unmanaged self-KO risk.

l2_recommendation: L2 RECOMMENDED. Multiple deck-specific L0 mis-defaults are structural, not calibration: (H1) unconditional Torrential Heart self-KO and (H2) last-Pokemon self-removal are catastrophic and cannot be fixed by threshold tuning alone; (H3) Munkidori energy mis-routing and (H4/H8) real-damage/pre-damage awareness require deck-specific perception. If P1 telemetry shows loss_share[deckout] dominant and H1/H3 firing (consistent with the ~24% WR + high-deckout + Munkidori-energy report), an L2 rule set (self-harm gates, type-aware fueling, real-damage promotion, dig-stop) is warranted over L1.
